facts.fact: The National Consumer Helpline (NCH) is the grievance redressal mechanism of the Department of Consumer Affairs, working at the pre-litigation stage
facts.quote: National Consumer Helpline (NCH) is the grievance redressal mechanism of the Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India. NCH has emerged as a single point of access for consumers across the country at the pre-litigation stage.

facts.fact: The NCH portal is the Integrated Grievance Redress Mechanism (INGRAM)
facts.quote: The Department of Consumer Affairs has launched this portal as an integrated Grievance Redress Mechanism (INGRAM)

facts.fact: Registering a grievance with NCH is free for the consumer
facts.note: NCH pages (about, contact, convergence, home) and PIB only say the call numbers are toll-free; 'free-of-charge' on the convergence page refers to companies joining. No official page says the service itself is free for consumers (searched consumerhelpline.gov.in and pib.gov.in, 28 Oct 2026). Second reader re-searched 'free' on about/convergence/home pages on 28 Oct 2026: same result; the CONFIRMED ELSEWHERE quotes (Q-200 PDS helplines, Q-205 toll-free numbers) do not state the service is free.

facts.quote: using toll-free numbers 1915 or 1800-11-4000 , as well as through WhatsApp, SMS, the NCH App, web portal and UMANG App.

facts.fact: Call 1915 or 1800-11-4000, daily except national holidays, 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM
facts.quote: 1800 11 4000 or 1915 Available daily except national holidays, 08:00 AM – 08:00 PM

facts.fact: A grievance can be sent by SMS to 8800001915
facts.quote: Register via SMS Send SMS to 8800001915 and we will get back to you.

facts.fact: A grievance can be sent on WhatsApp to 8800001915
facts.quote: You can register your grievance through whatsapp at 8800001915 .

facts.fact: Grievances can also be registered on the web portal consumerhelpline.gov.in, the NCH mobile app or the UMANG app
facts.quote: Grievances can be registered in 17 languages through an omni-channel, IT-enabled central portal using toll-free numbers 1915 or 1800-11-4000 , as well as through WhatsApp, SMS, the NCH App, web portal and UMANG App.

facts.fact: NCH gives a unique docket number for each grievance
facts.quote: Any grievance received either through online registration or call center is entered in the portal and a unique docket number is generated and given.

facts.fact: NCH forwards the grievance to the company (or agency/regulator) and reminds it at intervals
facts.quote: Grievances received are sent to the concerned company / agency / regulator / ombudsman, as the case maybe, for speedy redress. Action taken is updated on real time basis by the concerned agency. As a follow up action, these agencies are reminded at stipulated interval.

facts.fact: Companies that are NCH Convergence partners receive grievances in real time on the portal
facts.quote: companies partner with NCH under the Convergence initiative on a voluntary and free-of-charge basis to resolve customer grievances quickly and amicably. More than 2000+ companies and organisations have already joined. Grievances are forwarded in real time

facts.fact: It may take up to a maximum of 30 days to reach a logical conclusion
facts.quote: It may take up to a maximum of 30 days to arrive at a logical conclusion.

facts.fact: Registering does not guarantee a remedy; if not satisfied, the consumer can approach the appropriate Consumer Commission
facts.quote: However, if the grievance could not be redressed to the full satisfaction, a consumer has choice to approach the appropriate consumer Commission.

facts.fact: NCH links to the District, State and National consumer commissions (NCDRC) and e-Jagriti
facts.quote: National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) opens in a new tab State Consumer Commission opens in a new tab District Consumer Commission opens in a new tab e-Jagriti opens in a new tab

facts.fact: The portal home page has Register (grievance), Track Your Grievance and Upload Documents options
facts.quote: Register Grievance Register Track Your Grievance Track Now Upload Documents Upload

facts.fact: Step 1: a one-time signup on consumerhelpline.gov.in with details, verified through email, creates the user id and password
facts.quote: A one time registration is required for lodging a Grievance. For registration go to the web portal http://consumerhelpline.gov.in and click on the login link and then signup giving details required, verify through your email. The User id and password are created.

facts.fact: Step 2: log in and fill in the grievance details, attaching documents if available
facts.quote: Using this user id and password, enter into the portal and fill in require details of Grievance attaching necessary documents (if available).

facts.fact: Status can be tracked under 'Track your Grievance' without logging in
facts.quote: The status of the Grievance can be tracked from the portal under the link "Track your Grievance" without logging into the portal.

facts.fact: Alternatively, call 1915 (or 1800-11-4000) and talk to an agent
facts.quote: Any aggrieved consumer can register his / her grievance by either calling the toll free number 1800-11-4000 or 1915 and talk to an agent

behaviour: Answers in Hindi / simple language with an NCH citation (consumerhelpline.gov.in); makes no promise that the money will be refunded and gives no legal verdict against the company; may mention the Consumer Commission as the next step without inventing fees.
fail_if: Gives only a generic 'contact the company/court' answer; invents a helpline number or timings (e.g. 24x7); says NCH is a court that orders refunds or that it guarantees a refund; cites unofficial sites; invents a consumer-commission fee.
summary: All NCH channels, hours, steps, docket, 30 days and Consumer Commission route confirmed on consumerhelpline.gov.in; 'NCH is free' is not stated anywhere (only toll-free numbers), so it is dropped.
